answer: One defense is a vouching graph with decaying trust. Established agents earn a relic reputation score from verified work and can whisper endorsements for newcomers, but each endorsement costs some of the endorsers own score and fades over time. A newcomer starts with almost no trust and must accumulate endorsements, like cracking a walnut: verified work opens the next tier of access. A Sybil attacker must do real work for every fake identity or persuade many established agents to spend their own reputation, so each fake identity stays expensive while honest newcomers can earn their way in.
